title: Source snapshot
description: One source snapshot (data/findings/sources/<id>.json): its words, as facts with proofs (DATA-PIPELINE §2). Written by salvo agents; facts only, no key, effort, campaign or status.

wayback.description: Wayback captures (their timestamps date the captures).

commit.description: Repository commit of the snapshot, or null.

sha256.description: Saved file → its SHA-256 (the saved copies stay outside git).

published.description: Publication date of the source, or null if not stated.

anyOf.description: The source's publication date (default run upper bound, DATA-PIPELINE §5.1).

agent.description: Agent (or person) who wrote the file.

snapshot_of.description: Earlier source id of the same board, or null.

captures.description: Captures of the source (Wayback, commits, our fetches): measures name those carrying their value (value_seen_in); the earliest gives the run's default upper bound.

url.description: Capture URL (Wayback URL with its timestamp, commit URL).

captured.description: When the capture was made (Wayback timestamp, commit date, our fetch time).

file.description: Saved copy of this capture (a key of the sha256 map).

extractions.description: Text extractions of binary saved copies (PDF): quotes of facts in a PDF point at the extraction, where the validator finds them (NFKC-normalised).

file.description: The text extraction (a key of the sha256 map).

from.description: The saved binary it was extracted from (a key of the sha256 map), e.g. a PDF.

items.description: One fact: what the source says, with its proof.

id.description: Fact id, unique in the source (F1, F2...).

about.description: The source's entry name, verbatim (row label, model string as printed; for a chart point, the series' legend label, the marker going in `where`); null for a source-wide fact. Within a measure, the value and the per-entry facts (spend, usage, judge, anomalies) are about an entry a model fact names.

value.description: The value, verbatim as the source writes it (numbers as printed, with their % or $).

term.description: For fact types with a closed vocabulary (vocab closed_term_fact_types: score → metric, unit, currency, cost-basis, cost-method): the vocabulary term this verbatim value stands for; for a thinking-budget: its token count (digits); for a route: the routes.json id when registered. Re-derived by the verifier.

level.description: Certainty of the fact as written by the agent (DATA-PIPELINE §1).

form.description: Where the fact sits; prose, table-cell, label, code and image-text need a quote.

file.description: The saved copy holding it: a key of the source's sha256 map (required when the source has several saved files).

where.description: Locator in that file: page, line, JSON path, CSV row/column, chart marker px.

table.description: For a data-file fact standing for a table cell: the table id.

chart.description: For a chart fact: the chart id.

quote.description: Exact text; required for prose, table cells, labels, code and image text, and it must contain the value.

translation.description: English translation of the quote, if needed.

precision.description: Precision model of the value (an attribute, never a level).

step.description: Printed: one unit of the last digit, in the value's unit.

sd.description: Chart-pixel: reading sd in the value's unit (or computed from reading_px and the chart calibration).

scale.description: For score facts (required): how the value is written (fraction, percent, raw). Never inferred from the value.

namespace.description: For model-api-id facts (required): whose naming the id is written in — a routes.json id (maker-api: the maker's own ids; openrouter: OpenRouter slugs), or `prefix` when the value's head up to the first '/' names the route (Inspect / LiteLLM provider prefixes). Not the route the call took. See models.schema.json for the resolution rule.

run.description: For a run-score fact (required) and a failure / partial fact about one run: the run's id within the measure (a failure naming no run leaves the mean not recomputable).

note.description: Free note for the verifier; never read by the tree.

rule.description: For a computed fact: the rule deriving it (cell-difference: inputs[0] − inputs[1] − …; cell-sum: their sum; chart-effort-order: an effort-order fact 'k/n', inputs[0] the fact stating the chart's points are effort levels; complement-of-percent: 100 − inputs[0], a printed rate whose complement the setup holds).

inputs.description: For a computed fact: the facts or cells it is derived from, in the rule's order.

pattern.description: For a run-date-convention fact: a regex with a named group `date` (YYYYMMDD) matched against the measure's row key or run-id.

tables.description: Data-file tables standing for their cells.

items.description: A data-file table standing for its cells (DATA-PIPELINE §2): proven by the file's sha256 and this locator.

id.description: Table id (T1...). Its cells are cited as T<n>/<row key>/<column>.

file.description: The saved data file (a key of the sha256 map).

where.description: Where the table is in the file. format json: a JSON path ($, .key, ['key'], [n], [*]) to the list of row objects (or to an object of row objects, row_key '$key' = their keys); a column is a key of the row object or a dotted path in it. csv: free text.

row_key.description: The column whose value names a row (the `about` of its cells).

columns.description: Column name → the fact type of its cells (only the columns used need be listed).

additionalProperties.description: A table column: the fact type its cells state (string), or an object with the type(s) and, for closed-vocabulary types, the term all its cells stand for. A score column needs term (metric) and scale; a model-api-id column needs namespace.

says.description: The fact type of its cells, or several when one cell states several facts (an Inspect model string 'openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-27b' is both a route and an API id).

term.description: Vocabulary term of the column's cells.

precision.description: Precision model of this column's cells (overrides the table's).
Precision model of the value (an attribute, never a level).

step.description: Printed: one unit of the last digit, in the value's unit.

sd.description: Chart-pixel: reading sd in the value's unit (or computed from reading_px and the chart calibration).

items.description: A digitised chart: the calibration its read facts depend on.

file.description: The saved document or image (a key of the sha256 map).

kind.description: raster (pixels: points are read) | vector (paths: points are written, exact).

units_per_px.description: Fitted units (or log10 decades) per pixel.

fit_residual_px.description: Residual of the tick fit, px.

units_per_px.description: Fitted units (or log10 decades) per pixel.

fit_residual_px.description: Residual of the tick fit, px.

reading_px.description: Reading error of a point, px (from an independent re-reading).

checks.description: How the reading was checked (re-reading, printed cross-checks).

legacy.description: Migration: the CSV these legacy-row facts are records of (today's raw-data.csv).

file.description: The saved CSV (a key of the sha256 map).

source.description: The raw-data.csv `source` value of every row of this file.

decimal_mark.description: The source's decimal mark when it is a comma ('12,5'): the build reads its numbers so ('1.234,5' → 1234.5) while quotes keep the printed value (27 Oct).
